# Intake Brief — wl sync: guard the push side against sentinel worklog identities (SA-0MVKMVIAK005981E)

> Discovered-from: SA-0MVK4F993008D9S2 (during the SA-0MVB57M02008QPJS epic).

## Problem statement

`wl sync` quarantines *inbound* worklog commits authored by an incident-era sentinel identity (`t@t.com` et al.) — the author-identity gate — but nothing stops a checkout that still carries a sentinel `user.email` from *publishing* worklog commits under that identity in the first place. That is the 2026-10-22 incident (host `RossGameDev` pushed `T <t@t.com>`; every other clone refused to sync until the refs were re-authored by hand) and it recurred with two further inbound `t@t.com` commits on 2026-10-23 (`dec50d4d6`, `893203e8d`). `scripts/check_git_identity.py` detects the state but is advisory and fail-open (pre-push hook only) — a direct `wl sync` (as agent sessions run) has no guard, so the push side remains the durable gap.

## Users

- **Operators** syncing worklog data from any machine/checkout — a checkout with a stale sentinel identity (e.g. `RossGameDev`) must be stopped *before* it publishes.
  - *As an operator, I want `wl sync` to refuse to push when my checkout's identity is a sentinel, so I never strand worklog data for every other clone again.*
- **Agents** invoking `wl sync` directly in sessions — they skip the pre-push hook and currently have no protection.
  - *As an agent, I want the refusal to name the identity and the remedy, so I can fix `git config user.email` instead of shipping a poisoned ref.*
- **Every other clone/consumer** of `refs/worklog/data` — the pull-side gate keeps working, but prevention at the source means no more blocked syncs.
  - *As a syncing clone, I want sentinel-authored commits to never reach the remote ref, so my `wl sync` never refuses on inbound history again.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — A `wl sync` that would push worklog data while the effective `user.email` is empty or an exact incident-era sentinel refuses *before* pushing, naming the identity and the remedy (`git config user.email …`); the refusal applies when push would run (not with `--no-push` and not on the zero-change fast path).
- AC2 — The refusal never applies to the project's configured identity or to `syncAllowedAuthors` entries; the sentinel comparison is exact-email only (lowercased/trimmed match against the `INCIDENT_ERA_EMAILS` set: `t@t.com`, `t@t`, `test@test.com`, `test@test`, `cache test@test.com`), never a wildcard/substring match.
- AC3 — An explicit escape hatch (`--allow-sentinel-author`) permits a deliberate one-off push, mirroring `--allow-foreign-author`: it never bypasses the empty-email refusal and it is audit-logged in the sync output/log when used.
- AC4 — Regression tests cover the sentinel/empty/config-identity decision as a pure function (Cartesian over effective/configured email × allow-list) plus one CLI-level refusal test; no network.
- AC5 — Documentation: worklog sync docs describe the pull-side gate and the new push-side guard together (remedy, escape hatch, and why sentinels can never be allow-listed).
- AC6 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (ContextHub CLI suite for the new guard; SorraAgents suite remains green).

## Impact

Operators can no longer accidentally publish worklog commits under an incident-era sentinel identity, so every clone's `wl sync` stays mergeable and the manual re-authoring drill (2026-09-26, 2026-10-22, 2026-10-23) becomes unnecessary.

## Constraints

- **Cross-repo delivery:** the fix belongs in the **ContextHub worklog CLI** (TypeScript: `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/src/...`, released as the `worklog` npm package), while this item is tracked in the **SorraAgents** worklog because the incident surfaced here. The implement workflow's worktree isolation is repo-scoped — the delivery mechanism (linked ContextHub/WL child item vs. cross-repo delivery directly from this item, cf. SA-0MVZEO59E004BCI8) must be settled at plan time, *before* `implement.py start` (precedent: WL-0MUAD8U24001ZK5K kept this exact question open until planning).
- **Sentinel set parity:** reuse the `INCIDENT_ERA_EMAILS` rule from `scripts/check_git_identity.py` verbatim (duplicated in TypeScript — no cross-language import); keep both sets in sync via cross-referencing comments.
- **Escape-hatch symmetry:** `--allow-sentinel-author` mirrors `--allow-foreign-author` — never bypasses the empty-email gate, overrides config for that run only, does not modify `syncAllowedAuthors`.
- **No new dependencies; bounded, non-interactive; no network in tests.**

## Existing state

- **Pull side (guarded):** `ContextHub/src/sync/author-identity.ts` — `checkAuthorIdentity`/`enforceAuthorIdentityGate` refuse inbound commits whose author email is empty or foreign (allow-list `syncAllowedAuthors`, exact-email). Wired into `performSync` (`src/commands/sync.ts`) after the fetch, before any merge.
- **Push side (unguarded):** `ContextHub/src/sync/push.ts` — `gitPushDataFileToBranch` commits the JSONL export with the ambient git identity and pushes to `refs/worklog/data`. `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile` (the `wl doctor foreign-items --apply --push` force-rewrite path) commits and force-pushes the same way. Neither checks the authoring identity.
- **Advisory guard only:** SorraAgents `scripts/check_git_identity.py` (owner SA-0MUJ2VMF7000UHCX) detects sentinel/empty/mismatched identities, fail-open in `.githooks/pre-push` — a direct `wl sync` (the agent-session path) bypasses it.
- **Policy:** incident sentinels may never enter `syncAllowedAuthors` — pinned by `tests/test_author_gate_allowlist.py` (`test_incident_sentinel_emails_are_absent_from_the_project_allowlist`). Project allow-list: `250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com`, `pi@local`, `sorra@thewizardscode.com` (`.worklog/config.yaml`).

## Desired change

1. In the worklog CLI, before the push step of `wl sync`, read the effective `user.email` (same identity git will commit with in the temp worktree) and refuse — with the identity named and the `git config user.email …` remedy — when it is empty or an exact sentinel match. Applies only when a push would actually run.
2. Pure, deterministic decision function mirroring `checkAuthorIdentity` (same input → same result for dry-run and normal modes): inputs = effective email, configured/expected email, `syncAllowedAuthors`, sentinel set; outputs = allow / refuse + reason. Guard order: empty → refuse unconditionally; exact sentinel → refuse unless `--allow-sentinel-author`; otherwise pass (non-sentinel configured/allow-listed identities are never refused — exact-email rule, no wildcards).
3. New `--allow-sentinel-author` flag wired through `SyncOptions` → `performSync`; when used, the sync output and sync log record the bypass (audit trail).
4. Same guard applied to the shared commit path used by `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile` (force-rewrite path) so a sentinel identity can never author any worklog-data commit.
5. Regression tests: pure-function coverage of the sentinel/empty/config-identity matrix (unit, no network) plus one CLI-level refusal test (`wl sync` with a sentinel `user.email` refuses before pushing).
6. Documentation: `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md` updated to describe pull gate + push guard together; code comments cross-reference `scripts/check_git_identity.py` as the sentinel-set source of truth.

## Key Files:

- `ContextHub/src/sync/push.ts` — add the pre-push identity guard to `gitPushDataFileToBranch` (and the shared commit path used by `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile`).
- `ContextHub/src/sync/author-identity.ts` — add the sentinel set (`INCIDENT_ERA_EMAILS`) + the pure push-side decision function next to the existing pull-side gate (or a new `src/sync/push-authority.ts`).
- `ContextHub/src/commands/sync.ts` — wire `--allow-sentinel-author` (option, `performSync` options, audit log output).
- `ContextHub/src/cli-types.ts` — `SyncOptions` typing for the new flag.
- `ContextHub/tests/sync-author-gate.test.ts` and `ContextHub/tests/cli/sync-author-gate.test.ts` — pure-function matrix + CLI-level refusal (no network).
- `SorraAgents/docs/dev/worklog-sync.md` — document the push-side guard alongside the existing author-identity gate (AC5).
- `SorraAgents/scripts/check_git_identity.py` — canonical `INCIDENT_ERA_EMAILS`; cross-reference (source of truth for the TS set).

## Related work

- **SA-0MUJ2VMF7000UHCX** (completed, high) — *Restore wl sync: main-checkout git identity was left as incident-era 'T <t@t.com>'* — owns `scripts/check_git_identity.py`, the advisory guard this item makes redundant-at-source.
- **SA-0MV9JVLBQ0090RNC** (completed, high) — *Repair wl sync: allow operator GitHub identity, purge incident-era t@t.com commits* — established the pull-side allow-list/exact-email semantics this push guard mirrors.
- **SA-0MVK4F993008D9S2** (completed, high) — *wl sync blocked again: inbound t@t.com-authored worklog commits on refs/worklog/data* — discovery parent; the 2026-10-23 recurrence.
- **SA-0MVLJDS04002KI1W** (completed, high) — *wl sync blocked again: inbound t@t.com-authored worklog commits fail the author-identity gate* — 2026-10-23 second recurrence.
- **SA-0MVB57M02008QPJS** (completed, high) — *wl sync blocked: pi@local* — the epic this item was discovered during; `pi@local` allow-listing context.
- **SA-0MVVX9PAT009Q45H** (open, high) — *wl sync blocked: sorra@thewizardscode.com* — pull-side allow-list edge (deliberately allow-listed real identity — the carve-out pattern AC2 protects).
- **WL-0MUAD8U24001ZK5K** (completed, ContextHub store) — *wl sync to be run before refactor and standup skills* — precedent for cross-repo items and for recording delivery-location as an explicit question before implement.
- **SA-0MVZEO59E004BCI8** (completed) — *implement.py drive: refusal-aware finish recovery (cross-repo delivery record)* — precedent for delivering cross-repo work from a tracking item.

## Risks & assumptions

- **AC2 interpretation (recommended, pending producer confirmation):** the sentinel/empty refusal is **absolute** — it fires even when the sentinel email also equals the configured identity or an allow-list entry. AC2's "never applies to the configured identity / allow-list" carve-out protects *non-sentinel* identities only (exact-match rule); project policy already forbids allowing sentinels (pinned by `tests/test_author_gate_allowlist.py`), so the two clauses do not overlap in any policy-compliant state. Guard order enforces this: empty → refuse; exact sentinel → refuse unless `--allow-sentinel-author`; else pass.
- **Cross-repo delivery risk:** `implement.py` refuse changes outside the item's worktree; the fix must be delivered to the ContextHub repo through a linked item or cross-repo delivery. **Mitigation:** flag at plan time before `start`; record delivery mechanism as a decision in the work item.
- **Sentinel-set drift risk:** the TS set must stay byte-identical to `check_git_identity.py::INCIDENT_ERA_EMAILS`; no shared import exists across languages. **Mitigation:** cross-referencing comments + a unit test pinning the exact set (as `test_author_gate_allowlist.py` does on the SorraAgents side).
- **Escape-hatch abuse risk:** `--allow-sentinel-author` could be used routinely instead of fixing identity. **Mitigation:** audit-log the bypass in sync output/log (AC3) + docs frame it as incident-only, mirroring `--allow-foreign-author`.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "guard every git write in wl" is a tempting generalisation. **Mitigation:** scope strictly to the two worklog-data push paths (`wl sync` push + doctor force-rewrite); track anything broader as a separate item.
- **Assumption:** the effective `user.email` read at guard time is the identity git commits with — the temp push worktree shares the repo's config (including local overrides), so reading `git config user.email` from the repo root is sufficient. If a future git version allows per-environment author identity (env vars/`-c` overrides), the guard may need to consider `GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL`/`GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL`; out of scope today.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (AC2 scope — recommended interpretation, pending confirmation): "AC2 says the refusal never applies to the project's configured identity or `syncAllowedAuthors` entries. If a checkout's effective `user.email` IS an incident sentinel (e.g. the 2026-09-26 leaked-config state), must `wl sync` refuse anyway?" — **Recommended:** yes, refuse — the sentinel/empty gate is absolute and the configured-identity/allow-list carve-out protects only non-sentinel identities (guard order: empty → sentinel → pass). Rationale: sentinels are policy-forbidden from the allow-list (`tests/test_author_gate_allowlist.py`), so the clauses never overlap in a compliant project; a literal carve-out would re-create the incident. Source: AC1 text (`user.email` set to a sentinel → refuse), `.worklog/config.yaml` policy comments, `check_git_identity.py` remedy text ("incident sentinels such as t@t.com never"). Pending producer confirmation at review.
- Q2 (push-path scope — recommended, pending confirmation): "Should the guard also cover `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile` (the `wl doctor foreign-items --apply --push` force-rewrite) or only the `wl sync` push step?" — **Recommended:** both — either path publishes worklog-data commits under the ambient identity and a sentinel-authored force-rewrite poisons the remote ref identically. Source: `src/sync/push.ts` structure (shared commit path). Pending producer confirmation at review.
- Q3 (cross-repo delivery — flagged for plan time): "This SA item is the requirement/incident record, but the change lands in the ContextHub worklog CLI. Delivery mechanism?" — **Recommended:** implement via a linked ContextHub (WL) child item, or cross-repo delivery from this item per SA-0MVZEO59E004BCI8; settle before `implement.py start` (worktree isolation is repo-scoped). Precedent: WL-0MUAD8U24001ZK5K. Producer decision.
- Q4 (empty-email bypass — derived, no confirmation needed): "Does `--allow-sentinel-author` bypass the empty-email refusal?" — No: it mirrors `--allow-foreign-author`, which *never* bypasses the empty-email gate (documented in `src/commands/sync.ts` flag help and `src/sync/author-identity.ts`). Source: existing code, `--allow-foreign-author` semantics.

# Intake Brief — `wl sync`: file-lock age-expiry steals a live holder's lock (residual lost-update hazard)

## Problem statement

`acquireFileLock()` (`~/projects/ContextHub/src/file-lock.ts`) unlinks a lock whose `acquiredAt` is older than `DEFAULT_MAX_LOCK_AGE_MS` (5 min) **even when the holder PID is alive on the same host**. `wl sync` holds this lock for its whole fetch → merge → write → push operation, so a slow sync (>5 min: slow network, large store) has its lock stolen mid-operation; two writers then proceed concurrently and the sync writes back its pre-operation snapshot over whatever the stealer committed — the general lost-update class that WL-0MUV2U9QF002S9J1 closed for short operations. The claim-hold guard (SA-0MVE34D9B005TUYJ) prevents the user-visible reverted-claim symptom, but non-claim field writes are still exposed in that window.

## Users

- **Agents running long `wl sync` operations** (fetch/merge/push over a slow network or a large store). *User story:* "As a sync running longer than five minutes, I want my lock to stay mine for the whole fetch → merge → write → push, so a second writer can never run concurrently and clobber my write-back."
- **Auto-sync spawners and `wl sync --if-idle` callers** (herdr scheduling, worklist auto-sync). *User story:* "As an idle-gated sync, I want to skip (not steal) when a live sync holds the lock, so I never become the second concurrent writer."
- **Producers/operators and downstream gates** that trust the worklog store. *User story:* "As a producer, I want a long sync to never lose concurrent field updates, so `wl show` and the gate decisions stay trustworthy."

## Acceptance Criteria

- The same-host live holder is authoritative: `acquireFileLock()` must **not** remove a lock whose holder PID is alive on the same host, regardless of `acquiredAt` age exceeding `maxLockAge`. The two existing unit tests that encode the current steal-the-live-lock behaviour (`tests/file-lock.test.ts`: "should remove a lock older than maxLockAge even if PID is alive"; "should still remove an age-expired lock when skipIfLocked is set") are inverted to assert the lock is kept, and a new unit case asserts a same-host live PID with an age-expired lock stays in place.
- Stale-lock semantics are retained where PID liveness cannot be trusted: same-host dead-PID locks, foreign-host locks, corrupted/unparseable locks, and parsed-but-missing-field locks are still cleaned up exactly as today (existing `tests/file-lock.test.ts` cases keep passing unchanged).
- Deterministic regression proof that a sync's lock is never stolen mid-operation: a test in `tests/cli/sync-vs-mutation.test.ts` (git-shim fetch-parking technique plus a back-dated lock file — no sleep-based timing) holds a live sync with an age-expired lock and proves a second `wl sync`/mutation either waits on the lock or, with `--if-idle`, skips (`LockBusyError`); the parked sync's write-back is then the only write and no concurrent update is clobbered.
- The existing lost-update/claim-revert suites stay green: `tests/cli/sync-vs-mutation.test.ts` and `tests/cli/sync-claim-revert.test.ts` still pass; comments in `sync-claim-revert.test.ts` describing mechanism (a) ("the claim therefore acquired it") are updated where they describe the now-eliminated lock-steal path, without changing the suite's assertions.
- All relevant documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries; the full ContextHub test suite must pass with the new changes (excluding CI/CD pipeline tests; CHANGELOG.md is managed by the release pipeline).

## Impact

A slow `wl sync` can no longer lose its lock to a competing writer, so concurrent field updates survive long syncs and the worklog store is never silently clobbered.

## Constraints

- **Change site is the ContextHub repo** (`~/projects/ContextHub`, prefix `WL`) — the same cross-repo pattern as the sibling claim-hold children (e.g. SA-0MVKWV2V2006JC8E landed in ContextHub, commit `4eb0cc6b`). This item is tracked in the SA store; implementation and tests live in ContextHub.
- Surgical change to `src/file-lock.ts`; no change to the `DEFAULT_MAX_LOCK_AGE_MS` default (producer-confirmed scope A). Under the fix it governs only dead-PID/foreign-host/unparseable locks.
- `skipIfLocked` semantics preserved: a same-host live holder (any age) must yield `LockBusyError` → `wl sync --if-idle` skips, it never steals.
- Deterministic tests only — the git-shim parking + back-dating techniques, no sleep-based timing races.
- All lock consumers (`wl sync`, mutating commands, `wl unlock`, `withFileLock`) must keep the same mutual-exclusion guarantees.

## Existing state

- `src/file-lock.ts` `acquireFileLock()` (≈line 330): after the dead-PID check, an unconditional age-expiry branch removes any lock older than `maxLockAge` — "treat it as stale regardless of PID status" — even when the holder is alive on the same host.
- Two unit tests assert that behaviour: `tests/file-lock.test.ts:459` ("even if PID is alive") and `tests/file-lock.test.ts:311` (same, under `skipIfLocked`). They must be inverted by the fix.
- `tests/cli/sync-claim-revert.test.ts` mechanism (a) documents the residual hazard precisely ("withFileLock() treats any lock older than maxLockAge ... as stale even when the holder is alive and unlinks it"); the claim-hold guard masks the damage for claims, which is why this item is a *residual* hazard.
- `tests/cli/sync-vs-mutation.test.ts` already has the parking harness (git shim inside `git fetch`, release-file gate) that the new regression test reuses.

## Desired change

Make the same-host live holder authoritative (producer-confirmed scope A): when the lock's PID is alive on the local host, never age-expire it. Keep age-expiry for same-host dead PIDs, foreign-host locks, and unparseable/corrupt locks. The heartbeat refresh (scope B/C) is explicitly out of scope (see Appendix Q1).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Hung-holder lockout (same-host).** Removing age-expiry for a same-host live PID means a genuinely stuck (non-crashing) sync holds the lock indefinitely; nothing auto-recovers it. Mitigation: the manual `wl unlock`/`releaseFileLock` escape remains; the heartbeat option (scope B) was considered and deliberately **declined** by the producer (Q1 → A) — a heartbeat is a possible follow-up item, not added scope. Dead-process locks (the common crash case) are still reclaimed by the PID check.
- **PID recycling without a heartbeat.** A crashed holder whose PID is later reused could in theory look permanently live. Recorded as an accepted, practically-negligible risk (Linux PID reuse takes far longer than the window between syncs); producer confirmed scope A, so the heartbeat (which would eliminate it entirely) is out of scope and could be a follow-up.
- **Cross-host long syncs stay stealable** (age-expiry retained for foreign-host locks per the suggested direction) — acceptable in this single-host environment; noted in the appendix so it is a conscious choice.
- **Test inverts may look like regressions.** The two unit tests that flip expectation are the *correct* outcome of the fix; the brief pins their new expectation explicitly so review does not re-revert them.
- **Scope-creep guard:** heartbeat refresh (scope B/C), cross-host live-authority, and `maxLockAge` default changes were offered as Q1 options; the producer chose **A (minimal)** — none of the alternatives become scope. Heartbeat remains a candidate follow-up item if the hung-holder/PID-recycling concerns ever bite.
- **Assumption:** change site is ContextHub with SA-store tracking, mirroring the claim-hold sibling pattern (SA-0MVKWV2V2006JC8E).

## Key Files

- `~/projects/ContextHub/src/file-lock.ts` — `acquireFileLock()` stale-check branch: same-host-liveness authority before age-expiry.
- `~/projects/ContextHub/src/commands/sync.ts` — sync's `withFileLock` acquisition (≈line 800); no change expected for scope A, verify only.
- `~/projects/ContextHub/tests/file-lock.test.ts` — invert the two live-PID age-expiry tests (lines ≈311, ≈459); add same-host-live-authoritative cases (alive+old kept; dead+old still removed; foreign-host old still removed per direction).
- `~/projects/ContextHub/tests/cli/sync-vs-mutation.test.ts` — new deterministic regression test (parked sync + back-dated lock + second writer waits/skips).
- `~/projects/ContextHub/tests/cli/sync-claim-revert.test.ts` — must stay green; mechanism comments updated if they describe the eliminated steal path.

## Related work

**Potentially related work items** (via `wl search "file lock"` / `"lost-update"` in the SA store, and WL store lookups):

- **SA-0MVE34D9B005TUYJ** — `wl sync --if-idle` reverts actively-worked items (completed): the claim-hold fix this item is discovered-from; its guard masks (but does not eliminate) this hazard.
- **SA-0MVKWV26Y000G3B9** — Reproduction: sync reverts a held in_progress claim (completed): proved mechanism (a), the same lock-steal this item eliminates at the source.
- **SA-0MVKWV2V2006JC8E** — TTL-bounded monotonic claim-hold guard (completed, ContextHub `src/claim-hold.ts`, commit `4eb0cc6b`): defence-in-depth that stays after this fix.
- **WL-0MUV2U9QF002S9J1** — Fix lost-update race: wl sync clobbers concurrent mutating commands (completed, ContextHub, commit `ed0acc60`): closed the short-operation lost-update class; this item closes the long-operation residual.
- **SA-0MW7Z77KI005MK0B** — Audit runner leaves items open after a failing audit when a concurrent wl sync races its restore (lost update) (open): downstream consumer of the same hazard class.
- **SA-0MWFMUYHJ004Z18S** — Race-clobber restore regression tests (open): test-first sibling covering the audit-restore slice.
- **SA-0MVCF5RKF0099K4R** — Worklog: stale-lock detection and bounded backoff for wl mutations (open): complementary stale-lock work in the same file.
- **SA-0MUXA5ZNZ0019QY5** — Ship release must verify in-scope work items are actually closed (completed): records a real lost close from this race.

**Potentially related docs:**

- `~/projects/ContextHub/src/file-lock.ts` (header comment documents the stale-lock rationale).
- `~/projects/ContextHub/tests/cli/sync-claim-revert.test.ts` (header documents mechanism (a) — the residual hazard).
- `~/projects/ContextHub/docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md` (audit-restore lost-update context) — verify only, no doc change expected outside ContextHub docs.

*Duplicate check performed: no overlapping completed item found — related items are complementary (fix predecessor, reproduction, and downstream consumers), not duplicates.*

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Fix scope. `src/file-lock.ts` currently age-expires any lock older than 5 min regardless of PID liveness. Which scope should this item implement? **A) Minimal (recommended):** same-host live PID is authoritative — never age-expire it; keep age-expiry for same-host dead PIDs, foreign-host locks, and unparseable/corrupt locks. **B) Minimal + heartbeat:** also refresh `acquiredAt` during long syncs (protects foreign-host readers; removes the PID-recycling corner). **C) Heartbeat only:** keep age-expiry but make the live holder refresh the lock." — Answer (producer/operator): **"1. A" — minimal fix; same-host live PID is authoritative; heartbeat is out of scope.** Source: interactive reply to the intake handoff (question comment SA-C0MWGANT20005TAAQ, answered 2026-11-14).

- Research summary: inspected `src/file-lock.ts` (`acquireFileLock()` stale-check, ≈lines 320–350), `src/commands/sync.ts` (`withFileLock`, ≈line 800, `skipIfLocked` path), `tests/file-lock.test.ts` (two tests at ≈lines 311/459 encode the steal-live-lock behaviour; surrounding dead-PID/foreign-host/corrupt cases must be preserved), `tests/cli/sync-vs-mutation.test.ts` (git-shim parking harness reusable for the regression test), and `tests/cli/sync-claim-revert.test.ts` (header documents mechanism (a) — the exact residual hazard; its assertions stay green but mechanism comments may need updating). No heartbeat mechanism exists anywhere in the codebase today; the PID-recycling concern that motivated age-expiry is documented in the `acquireFileLock()` comment ("handles PID recycling and environments where PID checks are unreliable").


## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MVKWV2V2006JC8E** – TTL-bounded monotonic claim-hold guard (completed)
- **SA-0MVKWV46J007EM51** – Claim-hold regression suite and full-suite gate (completed)
- **SA-0MWFJS65O005JMJF** – Finish wait ergonomics: one bounded internal wait, no bespoke retry loops (open)

### Repository file matches
